/**
 * @name ReDoS in URL parsing
 * @description Checks for regular expressions that might be vulnerable to Denial of Service attacks.
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity error
 * @id py/redos-url-parsing
 * @tags security
 *       external/cwe/cwe-1333
 */

import python
import semmle.python.Concepts
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs

from DataFlow::CallCfgNode call
where
  call = API::moduleImport("re").getMember(["compile", "match", "search", "findall", "finditer", "split", "sub", "subn"]).getACall()
select call, "Potential regex usage in URL library."
findings.hypothesis: Inefficient regular expressions used for URL parsing can lead to Denial of Service.

findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name Extract Regex Patterns
 * @description Extracts regex patterns used in the codebase to check for ReDoS.
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity warning
 * @id py/extract-regex-patterns
 * @tags security
 *       external/cwe/cwe-1333
 */

import python
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs

from DataFlow::CallCfgNode call, DataFlow::Node arg
where
  call = API::moduleImport("re").getMember(["compile", "match", "search", "findall", "finditer", "split", "sub", "subn"]).getACall() and
  arg = call.getArg(0)
select call, "Regex pattern used: " + arg.asExpr().(StrConst).getText()
findings.hypothesis: Regex patterns used in the library might be vulnerable to ReDoS.

message.text: Regex pattern used: \Av\[a-fA-F0-9\]+\..+\Z
Regex pattern used: \[A-Z0-9\]\[A-Z0-9\]
Regex pattern used: \[A-Fa-f0-9\]\[A-Fa-f0-9\]

Regex pattern used: 
        # any character not in the unreserved or sub-delims sets, plus %
        # (validated with the additional check for pct-encoded sequences below)
        \[^a-z0-9\-._~!$&'()*+,;=%\]
    |
        # % only allowed if it is part of a pct-encoded
        # sequence of 2 hex digits.
        %(?!\[0-9a-f\]{{2}})

findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name Path normalization logic detection
 * @description Detects logic that might be performing path normalization involving '..'
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity warning
 * @id py/path-normalization-logic
 * @tags security
 *       external/cwe/cwe-022
 */

import python
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.DataFlow

from DataFlow::Node node
where
  (
    node.asExpr().(StrConst).getText().matches("%..%") or
    node.asExpr().(StrConst).getText() = "."
  )
  and
  exists(DataFlow::CallCfgNode call |
    call.getArg(_) = node
    and
    (
      call.getFunction().(DataFlow::ExprNode).asExpr().(Name).getId() = "split" or
      call.getFunction().(DataFlow::ExprNode).asExpr().(Attribute).getName() = "split" or
      call.getFunction().(DataFlow::ExprNode).asExpr().(Name).getId() = "join" or
      call.getFunction().(DataFlow::ExprNode).asExpr().(Attribute).getName() = "join" or
      call.getFunction().(DataFlow::ExprNode).asExpr().(Name).getId() = "replace" or
      call.getFunction().(DataFlow::ExprNode).asExpr().(Attribute).getName() = "replace"
    )
  )
select node, "Potential path normalization logic involving '..' or '.'"
findings.hypothesis: Improper path normalization can lead to path traversal vulnerabilities.

message.text: Potential path normalization logic involving '..' or '.'

findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name Find usage of '@' in string splitting or searching
 * @description Locating code that handles authority parsing by looking for '@'
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity medium
 * @id py/authority-parsing-at
 * @tags security
 *       external/cwe/cwe-020
 */

import python
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.DataFlow

from DataFlow::Node node
where
  (
    node.asExpr().(StrConst).getText() = "@" or
    node.asExpr().(StrConst).getText().matches("%@%")
  )
select node, "Found usage of '@' literal, possibly for authority parsing."
findings.hypothesis: Incorrect parsing of authority component in URLs (e.g. multiple '@' characters) can lead to SSRF or open redirects.
